headlines: MIAMI BEACH TIDES HOTEL SECURES $44 MILLION IN FINANCING
$44 MILLION DEAL BOOSTS HISTORIC OCEAN DRIVE HOTEL
BIG PLANS AHEAD FOR ICONIC ART DECO DISTRICT HOTEL
draft.article: Miami Beach's historic Art Deco district is seeing major momentum as the iconic Tides Hotel property lands $44 million in fresh financing. Safe Harbor Capital Partners secured the funding through New York-based Maxim Capital Group to move forward with plans across several key parcels. The transaction covers the historic 10-story Tides Ocean Hotel at 1220 Ocean Drive, which features 45 guest rooms and hospitality amenities. The deal also encompasses neighboring Collins Avenue properties at 1155, 1201, 1221, and 1225 Collins Avenue. Together, the Tides Village site holds three buildings with 95 rooms, restaurant and retail space, a rooftop pool, and a 148-space parking garage.

headlines: MIAMI DADE COLLEGE TRUSTEES TO MEET DECEMBER 15

draft.article: The District Board of Trustees of Miami Dade College will convene for its monthly session on Tuesday, December 15, 2026. Set for an 8:00 a.m. start, the meeting takes place in Room 2106, the James K. Batten Community Room, at the Wolfson Campus on 300 NE 2nd Avenue in Miami. Community members can also follow the proceedings online via livestream. Board members may discuss potential real estate deals along with rulemaking matters during the gathering. The proposed rule was originated by Vice President of Information Technology and Chief Information Officer Robert A. Parrondo. It received approval from College President Madeline Pumariega and Senior Vice President, Chief Operating Officer, and Chief of Staff Maryam Laguna Borrego, Ed.D. Requests for public hearings or amendment copies go through General Counsel Javier A. Ley-Soto within 21 days of notice.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE MOTHER ARRESTED FOR CHILD NEGLECT AT NW 81ST STREET
FOUR CHILDREN RESCUED FROM SQUALID MIAMI-DADE TRAILER
DISTURBANCE CALL LEADS DEPUTIES TO ABANDONED CHILDREN IN MIAMI-DADE
draft.article: Miami-Dade deputies arrested 25-year-old Leslie Quinones on four felony counts of child neglect early Friday morning in the 900 block of Northwest 81st Street. Deputies responded to a disturbance call around 12:12 a.m. and discovered an open trailer where three children slept unsupervised amid piles of garbage and moldy food. The dwelling had no running water, working air conditioning, or electricity, which had been shut off because rent was two months past due. Quinones eventually returned carrying a fourth child. The Department of Children and Families took custody of all four children, transporting them to Jackson North Medical Center for medical evaluations.

draft.article: A third suspect is in custody following the deadly October 4 kidnapping of 22-year-old Eddrick Malik Bethune from North Miami. Sheldon Diaz, 32, was arrested late November 5 in Tampa after Hillsborough County deputies clocked his car going 50 mph in a 35 mph zone. Inside the vehicle, deputies found active Miami-Dade warrants, $10,000 in cash, several cellphones, and a THC resin pen. Investigators say Bethune was ambushed outside the Aliro apartments at 14040 Biscayne Boulevard by armed men impersonating police officers with flashing red and blue lights on a gray Camry. After an apartment shootout and kidnapping, Bethune was shot multiple times and killed in the Redlands.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE SCHOOLS INVITE MICROSCHOOLS TO LEASE EMPTY CLASSROOMS
EMPTY MIAMI CLASSROOMS OPEN TO PRIVATE LEASING
HOW MIAMI-DADE PLANS TO FILL THOUSANDS OF EMPTY DESKS
draft.article:
The Miami-Dade school district is inviting independent microschools to lease vacant classroom space across local public campuses. After losing nearly 16,000 students since last year, officials are seeking new revenue streams while adapting to shifting family education choices.

Verena Cabrera, the district enterprise development officer, stated the plan offers supportive learning environments while making good use of taxpayer property. Operators currently working from homes or storefronts can submit proposals until Dec. 1, with agreements expected by March or April.

Miami-Dade already leases the former Biscayne Gardens Elementary School to a Jewish elementary school tied to the Talmudic College of Florida. Participating microschools will also share common spaces including cafeterias, gyms, and playgrounds.

headlines: DADE COUNTY WAS OFFICIALLY CREATED ON FEBRUARY 4, 1836
DADE COUNTY FORMED IN 1836
HOW OUR COUNTY AND FORT DALLAS BEGAN IN 1836
draft.article:
Our community marks a significant milestone that dates back to February 4, 1836, the day Dade County was officially created. The newly formed county took its name from Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River.

That very same year, Fort Dallas was constructed in the region. The fort functioned as a military base during the conflict of the Second Seminole War.

The events of 1836 linked the naming of Dade County with Major Francis L. Dade, the Miami River, and the military presence established at Fort Dallas during the Second Seminole War.
